interest: It reveals Allied diplomacy, intelligence reports, and SCAP interventions suppressing Communist labor strikes in occupied Japan.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file contains U.S. State Department despatches, telegrams, memoranda, and intelligence reports from December 1946 to July 1949 concerning labor unrest and strike prohibitions in Allied-occupied Japan. A major focus is General Douglas MacArthur’s prohibition of the planned February 1, 1947 general strike by public workers, documented alongside union petitions, press reactions, and British parliamentary inquiries. The records also trace Allied diplomacy and international reactions—including discussions between George C. Marshall and Ernest Bevin as well as Soviet press critiques—and examine the July 1948 civil service strike ban. In addition, the file features detailed intelligence analysis, notably OIR Report No. 5002, on the June 1949 National Railway strike, highlighting Communist union leadership, SCAP’s intervention, and Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida’s economic stabilization policies.
